"You are now working as a AAA-quality indie game development team consisting of:

- Senior 2D game developers
- Pixel art character designers
- Animation specialists
- Gameplay designers
- Mobile UI/UX designers
- Game audio designers

Your mission is to transform TEAPOT'S REVENGE into a polished, memorable, high-quality Android pixel-art action platformer.

This is NOT a basic school project or a simple browser game.

The game should feel like a real commercial indie game with its own identity, memorable characters, satisfying combat, beautiful environments and challenging boss encounters.

1. COMPLETE ART DIRECTION

Completely change the visual direction to HIGH-QUALITY PIXEL ART.

Visual inspiration:

- Metal Slug
- Dead Cells
- Shovel Knight
- Terraria (environmental inspiration)

Do not copy their characters, assets or exact designs.

Create a unique pixel-art identity.

Requirements:

- Carefully designed pixel-art sprites.
- Consistent pixel resolution and color palettes.
- Detailed character animations.
- Beautiful environmental tilesets.
- Pixel-art lighting and shadows.
- Atmospheric backgrounds.
- Animated water, fire, smoke, leaves and particles.
- Parallax backgrounds.
- Beautiful combat effects.
- No blurry sprites.
- No random pixel sizes.
- No generic circles and rectangles pretending to be finished artwork.

Use proper sprite sheets and frame-based animation.

2. REDESIGN THE MAIN CHARACTER

The main character is a heroic TEAPOT.

Do not make it look like a basic teapot with eyes.

Create a recognizable original character design:

- A distinctive ceramic teapot body.
- Expressive golden eyes.
- Small detailed arms and legs.
- A unique metal lid.
- Small adventure backpack.
- Decorative details and subtle battle damage.
- A memorable silhouette.
- A personality that feels brave, funny and slightly reckless.

Create separate animations for:

Idle, running, jumping, double jumping, falling, landing, shooting, reloading, dashing, parrying, taking damage, victory and defeat.

The character must feel alive.

3. ENEMY DESIGN

Create at least 15 different enemy types.

Examples:

1. Tiny walking tea monsters.
2. Flying mechanical insects.
3. Armored kettle soldiers.
4. Exploding candy creatures.
5. Sniper robots.
6. Fast jumping enemies.
7. Ghost enemies.
8. Shielded enemies.
9. Giant walking mushrooms.
10. Flying explosive drones.
11. Mechanical spiders.
12. Poison-spitting creatures.
13. Heavy armored warriors.
14. Mini-boss enemies.
15. Elite enemies with special attacks.

Every enemy must have:

- A unique sprite design.
- Different movement patterns.
- Different attack behaviors.
- Health and damage values.
- Hit and death animations.
- Appropriate sound effects.

Enemies should not simply run toward the player. Some should patrol, fly, shoot, defend, chase or attack from a distance.

4. ADVANCED COMBAT SYSTEM

Create satisfying and responsive combat.

Player abilities:

- Normal shooting.
- Double jump.
- Dash.
- Parry.
- Ground attacks.
- Air shooting.
- Weapon switching.
- Special attack.

Add a special energy meter.

When the meter is full, the player can unleash a powerful ultimate attack with a unique animation and visual effects.

Combat must feel responsive and rewarding.

5. WEAPON SYSTEM

Create at least 6 unique weapons:

1. Classic Tea Blaster.
2. Spread Shotgun.
3. Electric Lightning Gun.
4. Fire Cannon.
5. Homing Bubble Launcher.
6. Heavy Explosive Launcher.

Every weapon must have:

- Unique projectile sprites.
- Unique shooting animations.
- Different damage.
- Different firing speed.
- Different attack range.
- Unique sound effects.

Add weapon upgrades and unlockable weapon abilities.

Make sure weapons are balanced.

6. FIVE LARGE WORLDS

Create five visually different worlds.

WORLD 1: THE LOST TEA FOREST
A colorful forest with ancient ruins, magical plants, waterfalls and mysterious creatures.

Boss: THE ANCIENT BLOOM.

WORLD 2: THE CANDY KINGDOM
A beautiful but dangerous candy world with choc

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

content.text:
We need build a complete game from scratch in an empty repo. Need Android pixel-art action platformer. Given environment is browser-based (OMGithub with node start script). We should build a web game (HTML5 canvas, mobile touch controls) that feels like an Android game, perhaps PWA-ready. Need high-quality pixel art generated procedurally via canvas pixel drawing — no external assets. That's substantial.

Let me plan:

- index.html with canvas, UI.
- JS modules: game engine, pixel art sprite renderer (procedural sprite data / sprite sheet generation), parallax worlds, enemies 15 types, weapons 6, bosses 5, combat, mobile touch controls, audio via WebAudio synth.
- Five worlds with levels. Need boss encounters. We need scope manageable but rich.

Approach: single-page canvas game with fixed internal resolution 480x270 (16:9) upscaled with image-rendering: pixelated. Pixel art at 1x, scaled.

Art: create sprite sheets programmatically using pixel art definitions. We need detailed sprites, not generic circles. Use array-based pixel art strings for teapot frames (multiple animations), enemies; tilesets drawn with palette and per-tile detail. Could produce surprising quality with layered procedural pixel art and dithering. But 15 enemy silhouettes hand-drawn as pixel maps... doable with compact 16x16/24x24 maps. Time/tokens constraints. We can create sprite drawing functions that draw characters from primitives at pixel level — but requirement "no generic circles and rectangles pretending to be finished artwork." We need textured detail and recognizable forms. We can handcraft sprite pixel maps for teapot and key enemies; generate animation via rig transforms/squash/stretch plus limb offsets. Actually frame-based animation required. Could generate frames into offscreen canvases from draw functions with articulated parts, recording each frame — still frame-based rendering from sprite sheets (we can bake frames to sheet). Use "sprite sheets" generated at startup: each animation's frames rendered to canvas atlas, then drawn as frames.

Better: define characters as vector-ish pixel parts and bake frames. E.g., teapot body with spout, handle, lid, golden eyes, backpack, arms/legs. Draw at 3x internal scale? Internal resolution 480x270, character ~26px tall. Detailed pixel art. We can draw at pixel granularity with helper rect/pixel. Use low-res offscreen and disable smoothing.

Let's design game:
- Title screen with logo, animated teapot, Play/continue, controls hints, weapon select maybe.
- World map (5 worlds, lock progression saved in localStorage).
- Each world has 2-3 levels? Requirement "five large worlds" with bosses. Could do each world single stage comprised of several screens/rooms with boss at end. That's five levels + bosses. "Large" enough: level width ~4000 px, platform layout, enemies, collectibles.
- Mobile controls: left virtual joystick/dpad, right buttons (jump, shoot, dash, parry, special, weapon switch). Responsive, touch.
- Desktop keys A/D, Space jump, J shoot, K dash, L parry, U ultimate, Q/E weapon switch.

Combat:
- shooting projectiles, 6 weapons distinct.
- double jump, dash with i-frames, parry timing reflects projectiles & stuns, ground pound maybe.
- energy meter fills via damage/parry, ultimate per weapon? Unique ultimate effect (screen-wide tea tempest). Could implement per weapon ultimate distinct visuals/damage patterns.
- health hearts, checkpoints, weapon pickups. Upgrades: weapon levels gained with "tea leaves" currency; unlock abilities? Can add upgrade shop on world map using coins: +damage, +health, unlock weapons under progression. Need "unlockable weapon abilities". Implement weapon mastery: each weapon has level 1-3 bought with coins, plus unlocked perk at level 3 (e.g. piercing). Show in armory.

Weapons unlocked by worlds. 6 weapons: Tea Blaster (start), Spread Shotgun (W1 boss?), Lightning (W2), Fire Cannon (W3), Bubble (W4), Heavy Explosive (W5). Or unlock via shop. Simpler: after boss worlds weapons unlock in armory automatically; player can purchase upgrades.

Enemies 15 types across worlds, with behaviors:
1 Teacup Imp (walker, lunges)
2 Buzz Bea (flying, dive)
3 Kettle Guard (armored, blocks front, shoots steam)
4 Gumdrop Bomber (hops, explodes)
5 Sniper Spout (stationary, laser aim, shoots)
6 Jumper Bean (fast leaper)
7 Phantom Brew (ghost, phases, homes)
8 Shield Spore (shielded, advances, bash)
9 Mushroom Brute (giant, slams)
10 Drone (flies, drops bombs)
11 Clank Spider (speedy, ceiling drop, dash)
12 Venom Toad (poison arcs)
13 Iron Churn (heavy armored, charge)
14 Mini-boss: Sugar Golem / Thorn Knight / etc. (3 mini bosses)
15 Elite: Elite enemies with special (e.g. Void Chef) or one elite variant per world.

Bosses 5:
1 Ancient Bloom (forest)
2 Licorice Colossus / Candy Queen? The prompt truncated at candy kingdom. We can define:
W2 Candy Kingdom boss: THE LICORICE QUEEN? Or "SUGAR CRUSH TITAN".
W3: Ember Foundry / "THE MOLTEN KETTLE"
W4: Sunken Tea Temple / "THE DROWNED EMPRESS"
W5: Clockwork Citadel / "THE IRON STEEP"
Need five visually distinct worlds. Since prompt cut off, make:
1 Lost Tea Forest (green, waterfalls, ruins) boss Ancient Bloom
2 Candy Kingdom (pink, chocolate) boss Sugar Crush Titan
3 Ember Roastery / Ashen Foundry (volcanic tea factory) boss The Molten Kettle
4 Sunken Tea Temple (underwater-ish ruins) boss The Drowned Empress
5 Clockwork Citadel (mechanical sky fortress) boss The Iron Steep
At least final boss.

Backgrounds: parallax layers with procedural shapes; environmental animation: water, fire, smoke, leaves, embers, bubbles, rain.

Level design: platform arrays per world seeded; collisions with tile platforms? Simpler platform rectangles with pixel art rendered top surfaces and walls. Level width 3600, ground gaps, floating platforms, hazards (spikes, lava, water). One continuous level with boss arena at end. Camera follows.

Need assets: generated pixel art. Sound: WebAudio procedural music per world and SFX. Music could be a simple sequencer with bass/arpeggio/percussion per world; loop. Implement audio engine with oscillators, gain, filters. Sfx variety.

Performance: at 480x270, particles okay.

Need screenshot check with playwright? Environment says use playwright-cli; check. We can run preview server via start script? Runtime dir unknown. Let's inspect environment RUNTIME_DIR, node availability, playwright-cli.

playwright-cli - run playwright mcp commands from terminal

Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]
Usage: playwright-cli -s=<session> <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page
  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page
  fill <target> <text>        fill text into editable element
  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files
  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)
  eval <func> [target]        evaluate javascript expression on page or element
  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog
  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog
  resize <w> <h>              resize the browser window
  delete-data                 delete session data

Navigation:
  go-back                     go back to the previous page
  go-forward                  go forward to the next page
  reload                      reload the current page

Keyboard:
  press <key>                 press a key on the keyboard, `a`, `arrowleft`
  keydown <key>               press a key down on the keyboard
  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

Mouse:
  mousemove <x> <y>           move mouse to a given position
  mousedown [button]          press mouse down
  mouseup [button]            press mouse up
  mousewheel <dx> <dy>        scroll mouse wheel

Save as:
  screenshot [target]         screenshot of the current page or element
  pdf                         save page as pdf
